hub.feature.connection_status_bar.title: Connection Status Bar
hub.feature.connection_status_bar.descri: The strip below the title shows four live health dots: BUS (the local message bus that links Hub, Architect, and Visualist), STREAMER.BOT (the bridge to your running Streamer.bot at ws://127.0.0.1:8080/), HUD (the OBS overlay server on port 18080), and SQLITE (the local databank). Green means healthy, yellow means starting up or no OBS browser source has connected yet, red means offline, grey means nothing's registered. Hover any dot for the detailed status — connected client counts, registered layers, bus URL, database path. The current time ticks on the right edge.
hub.feature.connection_status_bar.where: Top of the Hub window, just below the title bar. Always visible.
hub.feature.critical_error_bar.title: Critical Error Bar
hub.feature.critical_error_bar.descripti: A red banner that drops in whenever a script logs a Critical Error. It shows the most recent message and a counter (e.g. 'SCRIPT ERROR (3x): …') if more errors fire in quick succession. Click Dismiss to hide it now, or wait — it auto-hides after 10 seconds. Treat it as a heads-up: open the System Log for the full stack and context, since the banner only carries the latest one-line summary.
hub.feature.critical_error_bar.where: Drops in at the top of the Hub window automatically when a Critical Error is logged.
hub.feature.websocket_status_footer.desc: The footer along the bottom of the window reports the live state of the Streamer.bot WebSocket connection. Green text means the bridge is up and chat / events are flowing both ways; red means the Hub can't reach Streamer.bot — open Streamer.bot, confirm its WebSocket server is enabled, and check that Tools → Settings → Streamer.bot URL matches.
hub.feature.websocket_status_footer.wher: Bottom edge of the Hub window. Always visible.
hub.feature.live_event_feed.title: Live Event Feed
hub.feature.live_event_feed.description: A rolling, time-stamped feed of what's happening on the stream. Each line is tagged: EVENT for stream events (chat, subs, raids, channel-point redeems), VISUAL for animations triggered by your scripts, ERROR for script failures. Three coloured filter buttons at the top — Stream, Visual, Errors — toggle each channel on and off; click again to bring the channel back. The feed keeps the last 400 lines and trims older entries automatically.
hub.feature.live_event_feed.where: Open from Windows menu → Live Feed. Docked as the centre document by default.
hub.feature.chat_monitor.title: Chat Monitor
hub.feature.chat_monitor.description: A live read-out of incoming Twitch chat. Each row carries a role badge — Broadcaster in gold, Mod in lime green, VIP in magenta, Sub in deep-sky blue, regular viewers in grey — followed by a short timestamp, the username in their Twitch colour, and the message body. The view caps at 200 lines and trims oldest first to stay snappy during heavy chat.
hub.feature.chat_monitor.where: Open from Windows menu → Chat Monitor. Docked on the left by default.
hub.feature.script_monitor.title: Script Monitor
hub.feature.script_monitor.description: Lists every .phx script the Hub has loaded from data/logic/. Each row shows the file name, when it last ran, and its CPU and RAM cost during that run. The checkbox on the left enables or disables a script live — unchecked scripts stay loaded but skip every event, so you can silence a misbehaving script without restarting the Hub or moving the file. The list refreshes every two seconds.
hub.feature.script_monitor.where: Open from Windows menu → Script Monitor. Docked on the right by default.
hub.feature.script_activity.title: Script Activity
hub.feature.script_activity.description: A traffic-light view of script lifecycle. Each row is a .phx script that has fired at least once this session, with a coloured dot — green when idle, yellow while running, red after a cancellation or critical error. The Last Trigger and Trigger Type columns show when and what most recently kicked the script off (Twitch.ChatMessage is excluded so chat doesn't flood the view). Right-click a row to set its execution policy: Queue (default — wait for the slot), Overlap (run concurrently up to the cap), or Discard (drop new triggers if already running). Today only Queue is enforced by the runtime; the picker is in place for the next sweep.
hub.feature.script_activity.where: Open from Windows menu → Script Activity. Docked on the right by default, alongside Script Monitor.
hub.feature.auto_updater.title: Auto-updater
hub.feature.auto_updater.description: The Updates section at the bottom of Settings shows the running suite version (read from Directory.Build.props), the matching GitHub release tag, and whether a newer release is available on GitHub Releases. Hub queries the Releases API in the background at startup so the status reflects what is published right now. Click Check Now to re-run the query; click Update Now to apply: Hub force-closes Architect / Visualist / itself, hands off to Phoenix.Controls.Updater.exe, which downloads the release zip, verifies its SHA-256, and atomically swaps your install root to the new build (the prior install is kept as a backup for 7 days before being pruned). The updater then re-launches Hub.exe directly. No git checkout, .NET SDK, or rebuild is involved — installations driven by the bundled installer / portable zip are self-contained.
hub.feature.auto_updater.where: Tools menu → Settings → 'Updates' section at the bottom.
hub.feature.settings.title: Settings
hub.feature.settings.description: The Hub's runtime configuration. Streamer.bot URL is the WebSocket address the Hub connects to (default ws://127.0.0.1:8080/). HUD Server Port is the local port the OBS browser-source overlay listens on (default 18080). Chat Action Name is the Streamer.bot action that forwards chat into the Hub (default PhoenixControlsChat). Bot Username is comma-separated; messages from these accounts are dropped before reaching scripts so your bot can't trigger itself — leave blank to auto-detect. Script Timeout caps how long any single script run may take in seconds (default 30, 0 = no cap). Max Chat Scripts and Max Webhook Scripts cap how many of those handlers may run concurrently (defaults 3 and 5; 0 = unlimited). Connection-related settings take effect on the next Hub restart; the rest apply immediately on Save.
hub.feature.system_log.title: System Log
hub.feature.system_log.description: Full scrollback of everything the Hub logs — System, Communication, StreamEvent, LogicExecution, VisualEvent, CriticalError, Debug — colour-coded by level. The window backfills with up to the last 2000 entries when opened so you can review what happened before you opened it. Where the Live Feed shows a curated stream-side picture, the System Log is the full firehose for troubleshooting.
hub.feature.system_log.where: Tools menu → System Log. Singleton — clicking again brings the existing window to the front.
hub.feature.run_diagnostics_tests.title: Run Diagnostics & Tests
hub.feature.run_diagnostics_tests.descri: Runs the project's automated test suite (dotnet test against Phoenix.Controls.sln) and streams its output into a console-style window. Useful for confirming the build is healthy after pulling updates or after editing logic. Exit code 0 means everything passed; any other code means at least one test failed — scroll back through the output to find the failure details.
hub.feature.run_diagnostics_tests.where: Tools menu → Run Diagnostics & Tests. Modal dialog.
hub.feature.toggling_panels.title: Toggling Panels
hub.feature.toggling_panels.description: Each dashboard panel (Live Feed, Chat Monitor, Script Monitor, Remote Devices) has an entry in the Windows menu. Click the entry to open the panel if it's closed, or close it if it's open. A check-mark next to the name shows which panels are currently visible. Closed panels keep their previous size and dock position when you re-open them.
hub.feature.toggling_panels.where: Windows menu — every registered panel is listed.
hub.feature.reset_layout.title: Reset Layout
hub.feature.reset_layout.description: Throws away the saved dock layout and re-opens every panel at its registered default position (Live Feed in the centre as a document, Chat Monitor docked left, Script Monitor docked right, Remote Devices auto-hiding on the right). Use this when you've dragged something into a state you can't recover from. The layout auto-saves to %AppData%/Phoenix.Controls/Hub/dock-layout.xml when you close the Hub and is restored on next launch.
hub.feature.reset_layout.where: Windows menu → Reset Layout (bottom of the list).
hub.feature.hud_overlay_server.title: HUD Overlay Server
hub.feature.hud_overlay_server.descripti: A small local HTTP + WebSocket server the Hub runs in the background to serve the browser-source overlay used by OBS / Streamlabs. The port is set in Settings (default 18080). Point an OBS Browser Source at http://127.0.0.1:18080/layer/<layer-name> to render the layer; visual.trigger nodes in your scripts then drive on-screen alerts and animations. The HUD dot on the connection bar turns green once at least one browser source is connected.
hub.feature.hud_overlay_server.where: Runs automatically on Hub startup. No window — health visible on the connection bar HUD indicator.
hub.feature.scheduler.title: Scheduler
hub.feature.scheduler.description: The background timer that fires Schedule.Cron, Schedule.RunAt, and Schedule.Recurring nodes from your scripts. It evaluates pending entries every minute, so you can wire time-of-day, recurring-interval, or one-shot triggers without writing your own loop. Schedule entries can come from the AppConfig.Schedules list or from in-script schedule headers.
hub.feature.scheduler.where: Runs automatically on Hub startup. No window.
hub.feature.logic_watcher.title: Logic Watcher
hub.feature.logic_watcher.description: Watches the data/logic/ folder for changes and reloads any .phx script the moment it lands on disk (250 ms debounce, so a noisy save event doesn't reload twice). This is what makes saving a graph in the Architect take effect immediately — no Hub restart needed.
hub.feature.logic_watcher.where: Runs automatically on Hub startup. No window.
hub.feature.script_engine.title: Script Engine
hub.feature.script_engine.description: The runtime that executes everything Architect compiles. When chat arrives, when a sub fires, when a schedule triggers — the engine picks up the matching event block in your .phx scripts and runs the wired actions: send chat, fire an animation, increment a counter, call a webhook, etc. You don't interact with it directly; you see its output through the Live Feed, Chat Monitor, System Log, and the visible side-effects of your scripts.
hub.feature.script_engine.where: Runs automatically inside the Hub. Disable individual scripts via the Script Monitor.
hub.feature.layer_runtime.title: Layer Runtime
hub.feature.layer_runtime.description: The Hub-side dispatcher that turns visual.trigger calls into rendered frames in OBS. Each .phxlayer registered by the Layer Watcher gets its own per-widget FIFO queue so back-to-back triggers can't trample each other. When a script fires visual.trigger / wait_for_visual, the Layer Runtime enqueues the request, sends a RUN_TRIGGER over the WS /hud/<id> channel to the live OBS browser source, and (for wait_for_visual) blocks the script until the browser echoes VISUAL_COMPLETE back.
hub.feature.layer_runtime.where: Runs automatically inside the Hub. Health rolls up into the HUD indicator on the connection bar.
hub.feature.layer_watcher.title: Layer Watcher
hub.feature.layer_watcher.description: FileSystemWatcher over the Hub's data/layers/ folder. The instant Visualist saves a .phxlayer, the watcher reloads the layer in-memory and broadcasts LAYER_RELOADED so any connected OBS browser source hot-reloads without an OBS restart. Mirrors the Logic Watcher pattern but for layer files instead of .phx scripts.
hub.feature.layer_watcher.where: Runs automatically on Hub startup. No window.
hub.feature.layer_registry.title: Layer Registry
hub.feature.layer_registry.description: In-memory map of every loaded .phxlayer plus per-layer browser-connection presence. The HUD indicator on the connection bar reads from here: yellow when no layers are registered or no browser is connected, green once at least one OBS source is live for at least one layer. Hover the HUD dot to see a per-layer breakdown — each registered layer with its active/idle state and the renders-per-second the compositor reported in the last second.
hub.feature.layer_registry.where: Runs automatically. Hover the HUD indicator on the connection bar for the per-layer breakdown.
hub.feature.hud_routes.title: HUD Routes
hub.feature.hud_routes.description: Per-layer HTTP and WebSocket endpoints exposed by the HUD Overlay Server. GET /layer/<id> serves the compositor HTML — this is the URL OBS pastes into a Browser Source. GET /api/layer/<id> returns the layer's JSON for the compositor to evaluate. WS /hud/<id> is the bidirectional channel for RUN_TRIGGER / VISUAL_COMPLETE / CAPTION_UPDATE / FPS messages. GET /asset/url?u=<encoded> proxies external image URLs through the URL Image Cache. POST /webhook/<name> accepts inbound webhooks (gated by AppConfig.WebhookSecret via the X-PhoenixControls-Secret header).
hub.feature.hud_routes.where: Auto-mounted when the HUD Overlay Server starts. Each layer is reachable at http://127.0.0.1:18080/layer/<name>.
hub.feature.url_image_cache.title: URL Image Cache
hub.feature.url_image_cache.description: On-disk cache for images fetched by Image.LoadUrl nodes. The first request hits the upstream URL and stores the bytes under %LOCALAPPDATA%/Phoenix.Controls/Hub/cache/<sha256>.<ext>; subsequent requests (and reloads of the same layer) serve from disk so OBS never re-downloads the same banner. Time-to-live is configurable via AppConfig.UrlImageCacheTtlHours (default 24h). The fetch path is hardened: only http/https, only image/* MIME types, magic-byte sniff, and a body-size cap from AppConfig.MaxAssetSizeBytes (default 5 MiB).
hub.feature.url_image_cache.where: Runs automatically with HUDServer. No window. Cache lives at %LOCALAPPDATA%/Phoenix.Controls/Hub/cache/.
hub.feature.live_captions.title: Live Captions
hub.feature.live_captions.description: Reads Windows 11's built-in LiveCaptions stream via UI Automation and pushes CAPTION_UPDATE messages onto the bus, where Caption.LiveCaption nodes can render the text on-stream. Polls adaptively — fast (250 ms) while the caption is changing, slow (1 s) once nothing new is being said — so it costs nothing when you're quiet. Requires Windows 11 22H2 or later. Set AppConfig.LiveCaptionsEnabled to turn the service on; set AppConfig.LiveCaptionsAutoLaunch=true to have Hub press Win+Ctrl+L on startup if LiveCaptions isn't already running. Captions stay on the internal bus by default; flip AppConfig.LiveCaptionsBroadcastToOverlays (opt-in) to forward them to OBS browser sources too.
hub.feature.live_captions.where: Runs automatically on Hub startup when AppConfig.LiveCaptionsEnabled is true. No window.
hub.feature.translation_service.title: Translation Service
hub.feature.translation_service.descript: Optional translator behind the Caption.LiveCaption Translated socket. The default provider is 'passthrough' (returns the input unchanged). Set AppConfig.TranslationProvider to 'http' to POST caption text as {text, target} JSON to AppConfig.TranslationHttpEndpoint and render the {translated} field in the response; AppConfig.TranslationApiKey is sent as a Bearer token if set. Any error falls back to the original text so live captions never go silent. Provider-specific shapes (DeepL, Google, LibreTranslate) need a thin proxy at the configured endpoint until provider-shape switching ships.
hub.feature.translation_service.where: Configured via AppConfig.TranslationProvider / TranslationHttpEndpoint. No window.
hub.feature.ai_suite.title: AI Provider Suite
hub.feature.ai_suite.description: Scripts can call out to AI providers through the AI.* node family. AI.Prompt sends a one-shot chat completion; AI.StreamText streams the response chunk by chunk so chat overlays can render a live typing effect (with optional MemoryVar to persist a conversation across calls). AI.Moderate runs OpenAI's content-moderation classifier over a string. AI.GenerateImage produces a DALL-E image URL; AI.VisionDescribe asks a vision-capable model about an image; AI.WithTools is single-shot chat with a tools/function-calling array. Provider routing is by Model prefix: 'claude-*' → Anthropic, 'ollama/<name>' → local Ollama daemon, 'cerebras/<name>' → Cerebras, anything else → OpenAI. Provider keys (OpenAIApiKey, AnthropicKey, CerebrasApiKey) and OllamaUrl live in AppConfig (config.json); a missing key surfaces on the calling node's Error socket so the rest of a chat handler keeps running.
hub.feature.ai_suite.where: Used from any script via the AI.* nodes in Architect's palette. Provider keys are edited in AppConfig (Hub's data/config.json, next to Hub.exe).
hub.feature.docs_nodes_tab.title: Documentation — Nodes Tab
hub.feature.docs_nodes_tab.description: Hub Documentation now exposes two tabs: Features (the existing catalogue of windows, panels, menus, and background services) and Nodes (a searchable browser for every PhoenixControlsScript node template — the same ~132 nodes Architect's palette ships). Pick a node to see its inputs, outputs, default properties, and per-socket descriptions; type in the search box to filter by name, category, or description. Useful when you're reading a script log or .phx file and want to know what a node does without alt-tabbing into Architect.
architect.node.bubble.ai_generate_image: Generates an image via OpenAI's DALL-E. Single-shot — ImageUrl carries the result URL once the API replies; Error carries any failure detail. Default Model dall-e-3 at 1024x1024; pass Size 1024x1792 / 1792x1024 for portrait / landscape, or fall back to dall-e-2 with 256x256 / 512x512 for cheaper iteration.
architect.node.bubble.ai_moderate: Checks Text against OpenAI's content-moderation classifier. Flagged is true when any category fires; Category names the worst-scoring category, or is empty when nothing fires. Useful for auto-moderating chat or AI-generated alert text.
architect.node.bubble.ai_prompt: Sends SystemPrompt + UserPrompt to an AI chat model and waits for the reply. Model IDs starting with "claude-" go to Anthropic; everything else goes to OpenAI (default "gpt-4o-mini"). The reply lands in Response; any failure lands in Error.
architect.node.bubble.ai_stream_text: Streams a chat completion. Response carries the cumulative text (updated as each chunk arrives); Done fires when the stream closes. AI_CHUNK bus events fire per delta so chat overlays / HUD widgets can render the live typing effect. Model prefix selects provider: claude* → Anthropic, ollama/<name> → local Ollama, cerebras/<name> → Cerebras, else OpenAI. MemoryVar (optional) names a databank key holding prior turns as a JSON array — leave empty for single-shot.
architect.node.bubble.ai_vision_describe: Asks a vision-capable OpenAI model about an image. Prompt is the question; ImageUrl is the image to inspect. Response carries the answer; Error carries any failure detail. Default Model gpt-4o-mini (cheapest vision-capable model); pass gpt-4o for stronger visual reasoning at higher cost.
architect.node.bubble.ai_with_tools: Asks an OpenAI model with a tools array. Returns either Response (plain answer) or ToolCalls (JSON array of {id,name,arguments} when the model decided to call one of the supplied tools). Tools input is a JSON-array string of OpenAI tool definitions. Default Model gpt-4o-mini.
architect.node.bubble.api_call: Quick GET against Url with no headers or extras. Response carries the response body as a string, ready to feed into Text.Format or HTTP.ParseJson. Use HTTP.Get when you need headers or status code.
architect.node.bubble.audio_play: Plays the audio file at Path through Hub's audio output. Volume is 0.0 (silent) to 1.0 (full). Done fires after the file starts playing; Error carries any failure detail (file missing, decode failure, no output device).
architect.node.bubble.audio_play_tts: Speaks Text through Windows' built-in text-to-speech engine. Voice is the SAPI voice name (empty = system default); Rate is the speech speed (-10 slow to 10 fast, 0 is normal); Volume is 0.0–1.0. Done fires after the utterance is enqueued; Error carries any failure detail.
architect.node.bubble.audio_set_volume: Sets the global Audio output volume to Volume (0.0 silent — 1.0 full). Affects all subsequent Audio.Play / Audio.PlayTts calls until changed again. Done fires after the level is applied.
architect.node.bubble.array_contains: Returns true when List contains an element exactly equal to Value. Case-sensitive. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.array_filter: Returns a new list containing only the elements that include the Contains substring. Case-sensitive. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.array_get: Returns a single element from List at the given zero-based Index (0 is the first element). Pure data — no flow pin. Out-of-range indices return an empty value.
architect.node.bubble.array_length: Returns the number of elements in List. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.array_literal: Outputs a hardcoded list from a comma-separated text value. Edit Items inline on the node body (e.g. "alpha, beta, gamma"). Pure data — no inputs. Use Array.Make instead when you need to build a list from wired values.
architect.node.bubble.array_make: Builds a list from up to eight values A..H. Wire the slots you need; unwired slots fall back to their inline default (empty string by default). Pair with Array.Get / Array.Unpack on the consuming side. Note: only A, B and C are emitted by the current exporter — slots D..H are silently dropped until that follow-up ships.
architect.node.bubble.array_push: Adds Value to the end of List and outputs the new list. Done fires after the append; the List output carries the new list (input list plus Value at the end) so you can wire it straight into another node.
architect.node.bubble.array_reverse: Returns the list with the order of elements flipped end-to-end. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.array_shuffle: Returns the list with the elements in a fresh random order. Useful for raffles or random-pick alerts. Pure data — no flow pin. Each evaluation produces a new shuffle, so cache the result with Var.Set if you need to reuse it.
architect.node.bubble.array_sort: Returns the list sorted ascending. Pure data — no flow pin. Leave Numeric off for plain alphabetical sort; turn it on to compare values as numbers (whitespace-trimmed; any non-numeric items are pushed to the end).
architect.node.bubble.array_unique: Returns the list with duplicate values removed, keeping the first appearance of each. Comparison is case-sensitive. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.array_unpack: Splits a list into up to five named slots (Item 0..Item 4) plus Rest, which carries everything from index 5 onward as a list. Only connect the slots you need. Pair with Text.ParseCommand for chat-command argument parsing. If you need more than five slots, chain another Array.Unpack off Rest to read slots 5..9, and so on.
architect.node.bubble.async_delay: Pauses this flow for MS milliseconds, then continues on Done. For seconds, prefer Flow.Delay (more readable for streamer-facing scripts).
architect.node.bubble.async_join: Waits for every branch started by the upstream Async.Parallel to finish, then continues on Flow. The join waits on the parallel block as a whole — there are no per-branch pins because the runtime always waits for all of them.
architect.node.bubble.async_parallel: Starts up to eight branches (Branch1..Branch8) at the same time. Each wired branch runs independently of the others. Unwired branches contribute nothing. If any branch fails, the others stop too. Pair with Async.Join downstream to wait for all branches before continuing. Note: writes via Var.Set inside a branch stay branch-local; use Public.Set when a value needs to come back out.
architect.node.bubble.async_timeout: Checks how long this script has been running. OnTime fires while fewer than MS milliseconds have passed since the script started; Late fires once the budget is used up. Useful for skipping slow follow-up work after a long delay or a slow DB call.
architect.node.bubble.async_waitforevent: Pauses this flow until a bus message with the matching EventType arrives, then continues on Received with the body in Payload. Times out on Timeout after TimeoutMS milliseconds. Use this for cross-tool handshakes (e.g. wait for Visualist to confirm a layer is ready).
architect.node.bubble.async_waitforvisua: Fires a Visualist widget's named trigger and waits up to TimeoutMS for the browser overlay to report it finished. LayerID is the .phxlayer filename stem (no extension); WidgetID is the widget's GUID; TriggerName is e.g. "onTrigger:greet". Done fires when the widget reports completion; Timeout fires if nothing arrives in time. Use Visual.Trigger when you don't need to wait.
architect.node.bubble.bus_broadcast: Sends a bus message to every connected tool at once. Type and Payload work the same as Bus.Send; any Bus.OnMessage whose EventType matches Type will fire.
architect.node.bubble.bus_onmessage: Fires when another tool on the bus (Hub, Visualist, Architect) sends a message whose EventType matches this node. Type and Payload carry the body of the matched message. Source and Target are wildcard filters: "*" (the default) accepts anything, an exact name narrows to that one tool. Use the filters when several tools emit the same EventType and you only want to react to one of them (e.g. Source="Visualist" + Target="Hub").
architect.node.bubble.bus_send: Sends a bus message to one named tool. Target is the tool name ("Hub", "Visualist", or "Architect"); Type is the EventType label that listening Bus.OnMessage nodes filter on; Payload is the body. Use Bus.Broadcast to fan out to every connected tool at once.
architect.node.bubble.chat_message: Fires when a chat message arrives from Twitch, YouTube, or Kick — the platform checkmarks on the node body pick which platforms it listens to (new nodes default to all three). Set Commands to a comma-separated list (e.g. "!hello, !hi") to only fire on those aliases; leave it blank to react to every message. Command holds the matched alias without the leading !, Args holds the remaining words as a list, User is a packed 7-element array [name, is_mod, is_sub, is_vip, is_broadcaster, color_hex, sub_months] (read it via Array.Get or Array.Unpack), and Platform carries which platform sent the line ("twitch", "youtube", or "kick").
architect.node.bubble.chat_overlay_clear: Wipes every chat row from the named chat-overlay widget. WidgetID is the chat widget's GUID.
architect.node.bubble.chat_overlay_push: Adds a chat row to a Visualist chat-overlay widget. WidgetID is the chat widget's GUID; Username and Message are the row contents; Color is a hex string like "#7fff7f" — defaults to that green when left blank. Pushed live to every connected OBS browser source.
architect.node.bubble.chat_peekrecent: Peeks at the last N chat messages the Hub has seen, without waiting for new ones. The Hub keeps a rolling buffer of the most recent 50 lines. Usernames and Messages are comma-joined lists in oldest-to-newest order, with the same length, ready for Array.* / Flow.ForEach. N ≤ 0 returns the entire buffer; an empty buffer returns empty strings. Doesn't consume — calling it twice returns the same lines.
architect.node.bubble.chat_waitfornext: Pauses this flow until the next chat line that matches the optional User and Command filters, or until TimeoutMS milliseconds pass. User filter is an exact-match username (case-insensitive); blank means "any user". Command filter matches messages starting with !{command} — the leading ! is optional in the filter; blank means "any message". Got fires when a matching line arrives, with Username and Message filled in. TimedOut fires when the wait runs out. Different from Twitch.ChatMessage, which kicks off a new script — Chat.WaitForNext pauses mid-script for a reply.
architect.node.bubble.convert_tobool: Converts a string to a boolean. "true", "1" or "yes" become true; everything else becomes false. The Default attribute is used when In is unwired or empty. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.convert_tofloat: Parses In as a decimal number. Accepts strings, ints, or floats. Returns the Default attribute (or 0.0) when parsing fails or In is unwired/empty. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.convert_toint: Parses In as a whole number. Returns the Default attribute (or 0) when parsing fails or In is unwired/empty. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.convert_tostring: Converts a value of any type to its string form. Accepts Int, Float, Bool, List or String. The Default attribute is used when In is unwired or empty. Pure data — no flow pin. Heads up: when feeding in a Float, wire it directly from a Float-typed source (e.g. a Math.Divide output) — going through an Int-typed wire silently rounds it and you'll lose the decimals.
architect.node.bubble.db_checkexists: Branches on whether a persistent variable Key exists in the database. True fires if found, False if missing. Distinguishes "never set" from "set to empty string" — unlike a plain DB.GetVariable + emptiness check.
architect.node.bubble.db_cleartable: Deletes every row in a user table. The table itself stays — only the contents are wiped. Use carefully; there is no undo.
architect.node.bubble.db_deleterow: Deletes a single row from a user table by its RowId. Done fires whether or not the row existed.
architect.node.bubble.db_deletevar: Deletes a persistent variable from the database. Done fires whether or not the key existed.
architect.node.bubble.db_fetchrow: Fetches a whole row from a user table by RowId. Found fires with the row bundled into Row when the row exists; NotFound fires otherwise. Read individual cells anywhere downstream as {Row.ColumnName}.
architect.node.bubble.db_findrow: Searches Column in TableName for the first row whose cell equals Value. Found fires with that row's RowId on success; NotFound fires when no row matches.
architect.node.bubble.db_getcell: Reads one cell from a row in a user table. Pure data — no flow pin. The output socket auto-retypes (string / int / float / bool) to match the column.
architect.node.bubble.db_getcolumn: Returns every value in a single column as a list, in row order. Pure data — no flow pin. Wire into Flow.ForEach or any Array.* node to iterate. Useful for dumping every entry in a leaderboard or user table.
architect.node.bubble.db_getvariable: Reads a persistent variable from the databank. Survives Hub restarts. Returns the Default attribute value if the key doesn't exist. Pure data — no flow pin. Use namespaced keys like "global.myvar" (one value for everyone) or "user.score" (per-user, indexed by the chat user).
architect.node.bubble.db_increment: Adds Amount to a stored number — pass a negative Amount to subtract. With Row left empty, it modifies the persistent variable named by Key. With Row set, it reads the cell at TableName/Row/Key, adds Amount, and writes the sum back. NewValue carries the new total. Amount defaults to 1 so a freshly-dropped node increments by 1.
architect.node.bubble.db_insertrow: Inserts a new row into a user table with one column/value pair. The new row's id comes out on NewRowId so you can write extra cells into it with DB.SetCell. Tables and columns are created on demand the first time they're written to.
architect.node.bubble.db_rowcount: Returns how many rows a user table contains. Pure data — no flow pin. User tables are named with the User_ prefix (e.g. User_Counter) and are created on demand by DB.InsertRow.
architect.node.bubble.db_setcell: Writes Value into a single cell on the row at RowId in TableName. Pair with DB.FindRow / DB.InsertRow to locate the row first.
architect.node.bubble.db_setvariable: Writes a value to a persistent variable in the databank. Survives Hub restarts. Use namespaced keys like "global.myvar" (shared) or "user.score" (per-user). For values that don't need to outlive the script, use Var.Set or Public.Set instead — they're much faster.
architect.node.bubble.discord_webhook: Posts a message into a Discord channel via its webhook URL. Set the URL up in Discord under channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks; copy the URL into URL.
architect.node.bubble.event_executor: Fires every time an Event.Trigger somewhere in the suite sends an event with this EventName. The dynamic output sockets carry the variables the Trigger passed in.
architect.node.bubble.event_return: Sends return values back to the Event.Trigger that called this event. Set EventName to match the Trigger/Executor pair and wire values into the dynamic input sockets — each one becomes an extra output on the calling Event.Trigger node.
architect.node.bubble.event_trigger: Sends a named internal event to every Event.Executor node sharing the same EventName. Wire data into the dynamic variable sockets to forward values; the Executor exposes a matching output for each. Use this to call a shared sub-routine from multiple scripts without duplicating logic.
architect.node.bubble.file_readtext: Reads the file at Path and returns its contents as a string. Path can be absolute or relative to the Hub's working directory. Content is the file body; Error carries any failure message (file not found, locked, denied) — empty on success.
architect.node.bubble.file_writetext: Writes Content to the file at Path. Set Append to true to append to an existing file; leave it false to replace the file. Parent directories are created automatically. Error carries any failure message — empty on success.
architect.node.bubble.http_delete: Sends an HTTP DELETE request to Url. StatusCode carries the response code. ContentType is shown here for consistency with the other HTTP.* nodes — it has no effect on DELETE (no request body).
architect.node.bubble.http_get: Sends an HTTP GET request to Url. Headers is an optional list of key:value pairs separated by newlines or commas. StatusCode, Body, and Error carry the response. ContentType is shown here for consistency with the other HTTP.* nodes — it has no effect on GET (no request body).
architect.node.bubble.http_parsejson: Reads a single value out of a JSON string by dot-path. Path examples: "weather.temp" reads an object key; "items.0.name" reads the first item of the items array. Pure data — no flow pin. Returns an empty string if the path doesn't match.
architect.node.bubble.http_patch: Sends an HTTP PATCH request to Url with the given Body — usually used for partial updates. StatusCode and Response carry the result.
architect.node.bubble.http_post: Sends an HTTP POST request to Url with the given Body.  StatusCode, Response, and Error carry the result.
architect.node.bubble.http_put: Sends an HTTP PUT request to Url with the given Body — usually used for replacing/updating a resource. StatusCode and Response carry the result.
architect.node.bubble.http_webhooklisten: Fires when an HTTP request hits the Hub at /webhook/{Name} on its built-in web server. Body holds the request body, Method the HTTP verb (GET/POST/...), Path the full request path. Use this to receive pushes from GitHub, IFTTT, Zapier or any tool that can post to a URL.
architect.node.bubble.kick_ban: Permanently bans User from your Kick channel. Pair with Kick.Unban to lift the ban from a script.
architect.node.bubble.kick_broadcasterau: Fires when the broadcaster's Kick account finishes authenticating in Streamer.bot. Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.kick_broadcasterch: Fires when Streamer.bot's connection to Kick chat comes up. Flow-only — no data sockets; use it to announce or re-arm Kick-side state.
Fires when Streamer.bot's connection to Kick chat drops. Flow-only — no data sockets.
architect.node.bubble.kick_channelupdate: Fires when the Kick channel's title or category changes. Title and Category carry the new values; OldTitle and OldCategory carry the previous ones.
architect.node.bubble.kick_deletemessage: Removes one message from Kick chat by its MessageId — useful inside a chat handler that filters specific messages.
architect.node.bubble.kick_firstwords: Fires the first time a viewer speaks in Kick chat during this stream. User is the newcomer; Message is their first line.
architect.node.bubble.kick_follow: Fires when a viewer follows the Kick channel. User is the follower's username.
architect.node.bubble.kick_getuser: Looks up a Kick user via Streamer.bot. Outputs Id, Login, DisplayName and ProfileImage plus the IsMod / IsSub role flags; Username defaults to the event's user.
architect.node.bubble.kick_giftsubscript: Fires when a viewer gifts a single Kick subscription to another viewer. Gifter is who paid; Recipient is who received the sub. For batch gifts, see Kick.MassGiftSubscription.
architect.node.bubble.kick_kicksgifted: Fires when a viewer gifts Kicks — Kick's on-platform tipping currency. User is the gifter; Amount is how many Kicks were gifted; KickName is the name of the gift; Tier is its tier. Requires Streamer.bot 1.0.2 or newer.
architect.node.bubble.kick_massgiftsubsc: Fires once when a viewer gifts a batch of Kick subs to chat. Gifter is who paid; Count is how many were gifted; Recipients is the list of receiving usernames.
architect.node.bubble.kick_presentviewer: Fires when Streamer.bot reports the current Kick viewer list. Users is the list of present viewers, ready for Flow.ForEach or any Array.* node; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.kick_reply: Posts a threaded reply to the Kick chat message named by MessageId. A reply still counts as a chat message, so the same 500-character cap as Kick.SendChat applies.
architect.node.bubble.kick_resubscriptio: Fires when a returning Kick subscriber renews. Months is their total subscribed months; Duration is the length of the renewed subscription period.
architect.node.bubble.kick_rewardredempt: Fires when a viewer redeems a Kick channel reward. Reward is the reward's title; Input is whatever the viewer typed; Cost is its price; RewardId identifies the reward. Requires Streamer.bot 1.0.2 or newer.
architect.node.bubble.kick_sendchat: Sends a chat message into your Kick channel as the account connected in Streamer.bot. Kick caps messages at 500 characters — longer messages are dropped with a log entry instead of being sent truncated.
architect.node.bubble.kick_setcategory: Sets the Kick channel's category by name; Streamer.bot resolves the name to the matching category.
architect.node.bubble.kick_setrewardcost: Changes the price of a Kick channel reward. RewardId identifies which reward; Cost is the new price.
architect.node.bubble.kick_setrewardenab: Turns a Kick channel reward on or off. RewardId identifies which reward; wire Enabled to a boolean to flip it from a script.
architect.node.bubble.kick_settitle: Updates the Kick channel's stream title. An empty Title is skipped.
architect.node.bubble.kick_seventvemotea: Fires when a 7TV emote is added to the channel's Kick emote set. EmoteName is the emote; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.kick_seventvemoter: Fires when a 7TV emote is removed from the channel's Kick emote set. EmoteName is the emote; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.kick_streamoffline: Fires when the Kick stream ends. Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.kick_streamonline: Fires when the Kick stream goes live. Title is the stream title; Category is the Kick category being streamed.
architect.node.bubble.kick_subscription: Fires when a viewer subscribes to the Kick channel. Months is their total subscribed months; Duration is the length of the purchased subscription period.
architect.node.bubble.kick_timeout: Times the named User out of Kick chat for Sec seconds. Sec defaults to 300; values below 1 are rejected.
architect.node.bubble.kick_unban: Removes an active ban from User, restoring their access to Kick chat.
architect.node.bubble.kick_untimeout: Lifts an active timeout from User in Kick chat ahead of schedule.
architect.node.bubble.kick_userbanned: Fires when a user is permanently banned from Kick chat. User is who got banned; By is the moderator who issued it; Reason is the stated reason.
architect.node.bubble.kick_usertimedout: Fires when a user is timed out in Kick chat. User is who got timed out; By is the moderator who issued it; Reason is the stated reason; Duration is the timeout length.
architect.node.bubble.kick_viewercountup: Fires whenever Kick reports a fresh viewer count. Viewers is the current count. This fires often — throttle heavy follow-up work (e.g. via Time.SecondsSinceLastFire).
architect.node.bubble.logic_and: Returns true only when both A AND B are true. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.logic_equals: Returns true when A == B. Pure data — no flow pin. A and B share a wildcard type — wire either side first and the other matches.
architect.node.bubble.logic_greaterthan: Returns true when A > B (numeric greater-than). Both sides must parse as numbers; non-numeric input returns false.
architect.node.bubble.logic_lessthan: Returns true when A < B (numeric less-than). Both sides must parse as numbers; non-numeric input returns false.
architect.node.bubble.logic_not: Inverts a boolean: True becomes False, False becomes True. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.logic_notequals: Returns true when A != B (different). Pure data — no flow pin. A and B share a wildcard type — wire either side first and the other matches.
architect.node.bubble.logic_or: Returns true when at least one of A OR B is true. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.logic_select: Picks A when Cond is true, B when Cond is false. Pure data — no flow pin. A, B and Value share a wildcard type, so wire any one and the rest follow. Acts like a ternary (cond ? A : B).
architect.node.bubble.macro_call: Runs a saved macro (sub-graph) inline as part of this script. Double-click the node to open the macro editor. The input and output sockets on this node are driven by the Macro.Entry and Macro.Exit nodes inside the macro. Use this to package up reusable logic — for events that should run independently in the background, use Process.Spawn instead.
architect.node.bubble.macro_entry: Entry point of a macro — only valid inside a macro editor. Flow and variable outputs here become input sockets on every Macro.Call that runs this macro. Wire values into the dynamic output placeholders to expose them as macro arguments.
architect.node.bubble.macro_exit: Exit point of a macro — only valid inside a macro editor. Variable inputs here become output sockets on every Macro.Call that runs this macro. Wire values into the dynamic input placeholders to return them to the caller.
architect.node.bubble.math_abs: Returns Val with any negative sign removed (e.g. -5 → 5, 7 → 7). Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.math_add: Returns A + B. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.math_ceil: Rounds Val up to the nearest whole number (e.g. 3.2 → 4, -1.8 → -1). Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.math_chance: Rolls a percentage chance. % Rate is the percent (0-100) — Success fires that often, Fail fires the rest of the time. For example 25 → 25% Success, 75% Fail.
architect.node.bubble.math_clamp: Returns Val limited to the range [Min, Max]. Anything below Min becomes Min; anything above Max becomes Max. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.math_divide: Returns A ÷ B as a decimal. If B is zero the division is skipped and Result is left empty (downstream readers will see an empty value). Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.math_floor: Rounds Val down to the nearest whole number (e.g. 3.7 → 3, -1.2 → -2). Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.math_max: Returns whichever of A or B is larger. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.math_min: Returns whichever of A or B is smaller. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.math_modulo: Returns the remainder when A is divided by B (modulo). Pure data — no flow pin. Example: 7 mod 3 = 1.
architect.node.bubble.math_multiply: Returns A × B. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.math_random: Returns a random integer in the range [Min, Max) — Min is possible, Max is not. For example Min=1, Max=7 produces a number from 1 to 6 (think "d6"). Max is never returned, even at the RNG edge cases.
architect.node.bubble.math_subtract: Returns A − B. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.obs_refreshbrowser: Reloads a browser source in OBS. Handy after saving a Visualist layer when OBS already points at the Hub's overlay URL — the new layout shows up without restarting OBS.
architect.node.bubble.obs_savereplaybuff: Saves the current OBS replay buffer to disk as a video file. The replay buffer must already be running in OBS, otherwise nothing is saved.
architect.node.bubble.obs_setfiltervisib: Shows or hides a named OBS filter on a source. Scene/Source identify the source; Filter is the filter name as configured in OBS; Visible toggles it.
architect.node.bubble.obs_setscene: Switches OBS to the named Scene. Currently relayed through Streamer.bot — make sure OBS is connected there.
architect.node.bubble.obs_setsourceposit: Moves a source to the absolute (X, Y) position on Scene, measured in pixels from the top-left corner.
architect.node.bubble.obs_setsourcerotat: Rotates a source to Degrees. 0 is upright, 90 is a quarter-turn clockwise, 180 is upside down.
architect.node.bubble.obs_setsourcescale: Sets per-axis scale on a source. 1.0 is original size, 2.0 is double, 0.5 is half. Set ScaleX and ScaleY independently for stretching effects.
architect.node.bubble.obs_setsourcevisib: Shows or hides a source on a scene. Scene is the scene name; Source is the scene-item name; Visible is true to show, false to hide.
architect.node.bubble.obs_startrecording: Starts OBS recording. Does nothing if OBS is already recording.
architect.node.bubble.obs_startstreaming: Tells OBS to start streaming. Does nothing if OBS is already streaming.
architect.node.bubble.obs_stoprecording: Stops OBS recording. Does nothing if OBS isn't recording.
architect.node.bubble.obs_stopstreaming: Tells OBS to stop streaming. Does nothing if OBS isn't streaming.
architect.node.bubble.obs_takescreenshot: Saves a PNG screenshot of Source (on Scene) to Path. Path should be an absolute file path on disk.
architect.node.bubble.process_entry: Entry point of a process — only valid inside a process editor. Wire values into the dynamic output placeholders to expose them as inputs on every Process.Spawn that calls this process (same idea as Macro.Entry → Macro.Call).
architect.node.bubble.process_exit: Marks a clean exit point inside a process. Reaching Process.Exit ends the process normally (no cancellation). Multiple Exit nodes are allowed; whichever one runs first ends the process.
architect.node.bubble.process_spawn: Starts a named process running in the background. Done fires immediately and the parent script keeps going; the process body runs on its own until it finishes or Process.Terminate cancels it with the matching InstanceId. ProcessId selects which process on this graph to spawn (authored in the Process editor, like a Macro). Wire values into the dynamic input sockets to pass them in as Process.Entry outputs.
architect.node.bubble.process_terminate: Cancels a running process by its InstanceId (the value handed back from Process.Spawn). The process unwinds at the next safe pause point — usually within a fraction of a second.
architect.node.bubble.public_get: Reads a script-run-wide variable named {public.<KeyName>}. Edit KeyName inline on the node. Pure data — no flow pin. Lives for the script run and is visible everywhere: parent script, Async.Parallel branches, called macros. Not saved to the database — use DB.GetVariable for values that need to survive past the script.
architect.node.bubble.public_set: Writes Value into a script-run-wide variable named {public.<KeyName>}. Edit KeyName inline on the node. Visible to every Public.Get in this script run, including parallel branches and called macros — writes inside an Async.Parallel branch DO merge back to the parent when the branch ends. Not saved to the database — use DB.SetVariable for values that need to survive past the script.
architect.node.bubble.queue_clear: Empties the queue, removing every entry at once.
architect.node.bubble.queue_length: Returns the current number of entries in the queue. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.queue_pop: Removes and returns the oldest entry from the queue. Done fires with the popped EventID and Payload when the queue had something in it; Empty fires instead when the queue was empty. Only one of Done or Empty fires per call.
architect.node.bubble.queue_push: Pushes an entry onto a queue. Entries are appended to a persistent variable (default "global.queue") stored as pipe-separated text. The queue survives across scripts and Hub restarts. EventID identifies the entry; Payload is its body.
architect.node.bubble.schedule_cron: Fires on a cron schedule while Hub is running. CronExpression has five fields: [minute] [hour] [day] [month] [weekday]. Examples: */5 * * * * (every 5 minutes), 0 9 * * 1-5 (9 AM Mon-Fri), 30 18 * * * (6:30 PM daily). Use * for "every", */N for "every N", 0-5 for a range, 1,3 for a list.
architect.node.bubble.schedule_recurring: Fires every IntervalSeconds while Hub is running. Count outputs how many times this node has fired so far (1 on the first run). MaxCount 0 means "unlimited"; any positive number stops the schedule once that many fires have happened.
architect.node.bubble.schedule_runat: Fires exactly once at the configured DateTime (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-01-01T20:00:00). Hub must be running at the moment it fires — past times are skipped, not retroactively run. Use Schedule.Recurring or Schedule.Cron for repeating jobs.
architect.node.bubble.state_delete: Removes a named state variable, putting it back into the "never set" state. Done fires whether or not the state existed.
architect.node.bubble.state_exists: Returns true when the named state variable has been set, false when it has never been set. Pure data — no flow pin. Distinguishes "never set" from "set to empty string", unlike a plain State.Get + emptiness check.
architect.node.bubble.state_get: Reads the current value of a named state variable. Pure data — no flow pin. Returns an empty string if the state has never been set.
architect.node.bubble.state_listkeys: Returns a list of every state variable currently set, by name. Pure data — no flow pin. Wire into Flow.ForEach or Array.* nodes to iterate.
architect.node.bubble.state_onchange: Fires whenever the named state variable changes value. OldValue and NewValue carry the before/after pair. Use this to react to State.Set without polling — for example, "when stream_phase becomes live, send a chat announcement".
architect.node.bubble.state_set: Sets a named state variable. State values persist across scripts and survive Hub restarts. If the value actually changes, every State.OnChange listening for this Name fires.
architect.node.bubble.state_switch: Routes flow to the case output that matches the current value of the named state variable. Edit Case A and Case B values inline on the node body; Default fires when no case matches.
architect.node.bubble.streamerbot_doacti: Runs a Streamer.bot action by its ActionId. Use this to call any action you've already built in Streamer.bot — TTS, sound alerts, browser-source toggles, anything.
architect.node.bubble.streamerbot_getuse: Reads a user record from Streamer.bot's local user database. Data carries the raw record; use HTTP.ParseJson to pick fields out of it.
architect.node.bubble.system_getdate: Returns the current local date, broken out into useful pieces. Date is the full formatted string (DD.MonthName.YYYY, e.g. 24.April.2026); MonthName is the English month name. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.system_gettime: Returns the current local time, broken out into useful pieces. Time is the full 24-hour string (HH:MM:SS); UnixTimestamp is seconds since epoch. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.system_log: Writes a line to the Hub's log window. Level chooses which channel the line appears under — valid values: System, Communication, StreamEvent, LogicExecution (default), VisualEvent, CriticalError, Debug. Useful for tracing your script while testing.
architect.node.bubble.system_startup: Fires once when the Hub finishes starting up. Use this to set initial state, prime variables, or send a "Hub online" announcement.
architect.node.bubble.text_builder: Builds a string by filling {Arg1}, {Arg2}, {Arg3} placeholders inside Template. Edit Template inline on the node body, or wire the Template input to override it at runtime (a wired value always wins over the inline default).
architect.node.bubble.text_contains: Returns true when Source contains the Search string anywhere inside it. Comparison is case-insensitive. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.text_format: Builds a string by substituting {A} and {B} placeholders inside Template. Edit Template inline on the node body, or wire the Template input to override it at runtime (a wired value always wins over the inline default). Use Text.Builder when you need three slots.
architect.node.bubble.text_joinlist: Joins a list of strings into one string, putting Separator between each element. Edit Separator inline on the node body (default is ", "), or wire the input to override.
architect.node.bubble.text_length: Returns the number of characters in In. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.text_parsecommand: Splits a chat command message into Segments parts on spaces. The leading ! is stripped from the first word. The last segment soaks up everything left over. Pair with Array.Unpack to read the parts. Example: "!cmd add Test hello world" with Segments=3 → [cmd, add, "Test hello world"].
architect.node.bubble.text_replace: Replaces every occurrence of Find inside Source with With. Case-sensitive. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.text_split: Splits Source into a list of parts wherever Delimiter appears. Edit Delimiter inline on the node body (default is comma), or wire the input to override.
architect.node.bubble.text_tolower: Converts the string to all lower case. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.text_toupper: Converts the string to ALL UPPER CASE. Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.time_secondssincel: Returns the seconds elapsed since this Key was last checked, then stamps a fresh timestamp on the same call. Use any unique string for Key (usually the alert or command name) to throttle alerts globally or per-user. Pure data — no flow pin. Heads up: reading the output also updates the timestamp, so wiring it to multiple consumers gives ~0 after the first read. Cache the value via Var.Set if you need it more than once. On the very first read for a Key, returns a huge value (effectively "never fired").
architect.node.bubble.twitch_announcemen: Posts a highlighted channel announcement in chat. Color must be one of: blue, green, orange, purple, or primary (channel's brand color). Leave Color blank to use "primary".
architect.node.bubble.twitch_ban: Permanently bans User from the channel. Reason is an optional note shown in the moderation log.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_chatmessage: Fires when a viewer sends a chat message. Set Commands to a comma-separated list (e.g. "!hello, !hi") to only fire on those aliases; leave it blank to react to every message. Command holds the matched alias without the leading !. Args holds the remaining words as a list (use Array.Get or Flow.ForEach). User is a packed 7-element array [name, is_mod, is_sub, is_vip, is_broadcaster, color_hex, sub_months] — feed it through Array.Get or Array.Unpack to read individual fields.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_checkrole: Reports a viewer's role flags: IsMod, IsSub, IsVip, IsBroadcaster. Wire Username to test someone other than the event's user. Useful for permission gates ("only mods can use this command").
architect.node.bubble.twitch_cheer: Fires when a viewer cheers with Bits. Bits is the total amount cheered; Message is the cheer's chat text (may include cheermote tokens like Cheer100).
architect.node.bubble.twitch_createclip: Asks Twitch to clip the last ~30 seconds of the stream. Delay adds a 5-second buffer so the clip starts a moment earlier — useful when you want to catch the lead-up to a moment. Fire-and-forget: the clip lands in the Twitch dashboard a few seconds later.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_createpoll: Creates a Twitch poll on the channel. Choices is a comma-separated list of options (2-5 entries); DurationSec is how long the poll stays open.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_createpredi: Creates a Twitch channel-points prediction with two outcomes. DurationSec is how long viewers have to lock in their guess.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_deletemessa: Removes one chat message from chat by its MessageId — useful inside a Twitch.ChatMessage handler that wants to filter specific messages.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_endpoll: Closes the active Twitch poll early. PollId is optional; Streamer.bot ends the currently-open poll.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_follow: Fires when a viewer follows the channel. User is the follower's username.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_followermod: Turns on follower-only chat with a minimum follow age in Minutes. Pass -1 to turn follower-only mode off.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_fulfillrede: Marks a Channel Points redemption as fulfilled — clears it out of the streamer's queue. RedemptionId identifies which redemption (e.g. from a Twitch.PointRedeem event).
architect.node.bubble.twitch_getfollowag: Returns how long Username has followed the channel. Days is the raw day count; Formatted is a human-readable string like "3 months 2 days". Empty Days when the user isn't following.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_getstream: Reads live stream info for a Twitch channel. Leave Username empty to look up the broadcaster's own channel. Outputs the current Title, Category (game), live ViewerCount and Uptime (e.g. "1h 23m"). Empty values mean the channel is offline.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_getuser: Looks up a Twitch user via Streamer.bot. Wire Username from a command argument, or leave it empty to default to the event's user. Outputs the user's display name, role flags (mod/sub/VIP), sub tier and months, follow date, and account creation date.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_getviewers: Pulls the current chatter list from Streamer.bot. Viewers is a list of usernames ready to feed into Flow.ForEach or any Array.* node. Useful for raffle-style commands.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_giftbomb: Fires once when a viewer gifts a batch of subs to chat. Count is how many were gifted in the bomb. Use for celebrating big gifters; individual recipients still raise their own Twitch.Subscription events.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_giftsub: Fires when a viewer gifts a single subscription to another viewer. Use this for one-off thank-yous; for mass-gifting bombs, see Twitch.GiftBomb.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_lastactive: Branches on how long ago Username last chatted. Inactive fires when the gap is more than Minutes; Active fires when it's less. MinutesAgo carries the actual gap in minutes, or -1 if the user hasn't chatted this session.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_marker: Drops a stream marker at the current moment so it's easy to find later in the VOD. Description is an optional label.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_pointredeem: Fires when a viewer redeems a Channel Point reward. Reward is the reward's title; Input is whatever the viewer typed (empty for rewards that don't ask for input).
architect.node.bubble.twitch_raid: Fires when another streamer raids the channel. User is the raider's username; Viewers is how many people they brought. Common pattern: shoutout the raider with Twitch.Shoutout.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_rejectredem: Rejects a Channel Points redemption and refunds the points to the viewer. RedemptionId identifies which redemption.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_resolvepred: Resolves a Twitch prediction by declaring which outcome won. PredictionId identifies the prediction; WinningOutcomeId is the ID of the winning option.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_resub: Fires when a returning subscriber resubs and shares a streak message. Months is the total streak; Message is whatever they typed in the share dialog (may be empty).
architect.node.bubble.twitch_sendchat: Sends a chat message into the Twitch channel as the bot account configured in Hub.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_setrewarden: Turns a Channel Points reward on or off in the rewards menu. RewardId identifies which reward; wire Enabled to a boolean to flip it from a script.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_shoutout: Posts a Twitch shoutout for User — surfaces them as a recommended channel in chat. Common pattern: shout out a raider after a Twitch.Raid event.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_slowmode: Turns on chat slow mode with a per-viewer message cooldown of Seconds. Pass 0 to turn slow mode off entirely.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_subonlymode: Turns subscriber-only chat on or off. Wire Enabled to a boolean to flip it from a script.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_subscriptio: Fires when a viewer subscribes for the first time. Months is the announced sub streak (usually 1); Tier is "1000", "2000", or "3000".
architect.node.bubble.twitch_timeout: Times the named User out from chat for Sec seconds. Sec defaults to 60 when unwired or unset. Heads up: the Hub currently doesn't reject 0 or negative Sec values — pass an explicit positive integer for predictable behaviour.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_unban: Removes an active ban from User, restoring their access to chat.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_updatechann: Updates the live stream's metadata. Title is the new stream title (leave empty to keep the current title); GameId is the Twitch category/game ID (leave empty to keep the current category).
architect.node.bubble.twitch_updaterewar: Changes the Channel Points cost of a reward. RewardId identifies which reward; Cost is the new price.
architect.node.bubble.twitch_whisper: Sends a private whisper (DM) to User. Subject to Twitch's strict whisper rate limits — don't loop this for many users in a row.
architect.node.bubble.value_bool: Outputs a fixed boolean (true or false). Edit Value inline on the node body. Wire the Input socket to override the inline value at runtime (a wired value always wins). Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.value_float: Outputs a fixed decimal number. Edit Value inline on the node body. Wire the Input socket to override the inline value at runtime (a wired value always wins). Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.value_int: Outputs a fixed whole number. Edit Value inline on the node body. Wire the Input socket to override the inline value at runtime (a wired value always wins). Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.value_string: Outputs a fixed string. Edit Value inline on the node body. Wire the Input socket to override the inline value at runtime (a wired value always wins). Pure data — no flow pin.
architect.node.bubble.var_get: Reads a local script variable named {var.<VariableName>}. Edit VariableName inline on the node. Pure data — no flow pin. Branch-local: a value written inside an Async.Parallel branch does NOT leak back to the parent script. Use Public.Get when a branch needs to share the value, or DB.GetVariable for values that survive the script run.
architect.node.bubble.var_set: Writes Value into a local script variable named {var.<VariableName>}. Edit VariableName inline on the node. Branch-local: writes inside an Async.Parallel branch do NOT merge back to the parent — they vanish when the branch ends. Use Public.Set when a branch needs to share the value with the rest of the script, or DB.SetVariable for values that survive the script run.
architect.node.bubble.visual_trigger: Fires a Visualist widget's named trigger and continues immediately — does not wait for the overlay to finish. Use Async.WaitForVisual when you need to wait. LayerID is the .phxlayer filename stem (no extension); WidgetID is the widget's GUID; TriggerName is e.g. "onTrigger:greet". Wire a list (Array.Make / Array.Literal) into Args to deliver positional values; widget-side nodes reference them as {Args1}, {Args2}, {ArgsN} in Text.Render and as the When attribute on Result.If. Wire values into the dynamic input sockets — each socket's name becomes a key in the trigger's EventData on the widget side.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_ban: Permanently hides User from your YouTube live chat. There is no unban from inside Phoenix — lift the ban in YouTube Studio.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_betterttve: Fires when a BetterTTV emote is added to the channel's YouTube emote set. EmoteName is the emote; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
Fires when a BetterTTV emote is removed from the channel's YouTube emote set. EmoteName is the emote; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_broadcasta: Fires when a new broadcast is created or scheduled on the YouTube channel. Title, BroadcastId, Privacy, and Status describe the new broadcast.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_broadcaste: Fires when a YouTube broadcast ends. Title, BroadcastId, Privacy, and Status describe the broadcast that just finished.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_broadcastm: Fires when Streamer.bot stops monitoring a YouTube broadcast. Title and BroadcastId identify the broadcast; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
Fires when Streamer.bot starts monitoring a YouTube broadcast. Title and BroadcastId identify the broadcast; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_broadcastr: Fires when a broadcast is removed from the YouTube channel. Title, BroadcastId, Privacy, and Status describe the removed broadcast.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_broadcasts: Fires when a YouTube broadcast goes live. Title, BroadcastId, Privacy, and Status describe the broadcast that just started.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_broadcastu: Fires when a broadcast's metadata changes on the YouTube channel. Title, BroadcastId, Privacy, and Status carry the updated values.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_createpoll: Creates a poll in your YouTube live chat. Choices is a comma-separated list of options; DurationSec is how long the poll stays open (default 60).
architect.node.bubble.youtube_endpoll: Ends the currently active YouTube poll. Takes no inputs — Streamer.bot closes whichever poll is open.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_firstwords: Fires the first time a viewer speaks in YouTube Live chat during this stream. User is the newcomer; Message is their first line.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_getuser: Looks up a YouTube user via Streamer.bot. Outputs Id, DisplayName and ProfileImage plus the IsMod / IsSub (member) / IsBroadcaster (channel owner) role flags; Username defaults to the event's user.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_giftmember: Fires once for each viewer who receives a gifted YouTube membership. User is the recipient; Gifter is who paid for it; Tier is the gifted level.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_jewelsgift: Fires when a viewer gifts Jewels on YouTube. User is the gifter; Amount is the gifted amount; Payload carries the raw event JSON. Requires Streamer.bot 1.0.5 or newer.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_membermile: Fires when a member celebrates a membership milestone in YouTube Live chat. Level is the membership level; Months is the total months celebrated; Message is the optional milestone text they shared.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_membership: Fires when a viewer gifts channel memberships on YouTube. User is the gifter; Count is how many memberships were gifted; Tier is the gifted level. Each recipient also raises their own YouTube.GiftMembershipReceived event.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_message: Fires when a message arrives in YouTube Live chat (only when YouTube is connected through Streamer.bot).
architect.node.bubble.youtube_messagedel: Fires when a message is deleted from YouTube Live chat. User is the author of the deleted message; MessageId identifies it; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_newsponsor: Fires when a viewer becomes a channel member on YouTube. User is the new member; Level is the membership level name; IsUpgrade is true when an existing member upgraded to a higher level.
Fires when members-only chat is turned off for the YouTube broadcast. Payload carries the raw event JSON.
Fires when members-only chat is turned on for the YouTube broadcast. Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_newsubscri: Fires when someone subscribes to the YouTube channel. User is the new subscriber; Payload carries the raw event JSON for anything beyond that.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_pollclosed: Fires when the YouTube poll closes. Title is the poll question; Payload carries the raw poll JSON with the final results.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_pollstarte: Fires when a poll opens in YouTube Live chat. Title is the poll question; Payload carries the raw poll JSON (option details ride in there).
architect.node.bubble.youtube_pollupdate: Fires when the running YouTube poll updates (fresh votes). Title is the poll question; Payload carries the raw poll JSON with the current tallies.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_presentvie: Fires when Streamer.bot reports the current YouTube viewer list. Users is the list of present viewers, ready for Flow.ForEach or any Array.* node; IsLive says whether the broadcast is currently live.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_sendchat: Sends a chat message into your YouTube live chat as the account connected in Streamer.bot. YouTube caps messages at 200 characters — longer messages are dropped with a log entry instead of being sent truncated.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_setdescrip: Updates the running YouTube broadcast's description. An empty Description is skipped.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_settitle: Updates the running YouTube broadcast's title. An empty Title is skipped.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_seventvemo: Fires when a 7TV emote is added to the channel's YouTube emote set. EmoteName is the emote; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
Fires when a 7TV emote is removed from the channel's YouTube emote set. EmoteName is the emote; Payload carries the raw event JSON.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_statistics: Fires when YouTube refreshes the broadcast statistics. Viewers is the current concurrent-viewer count; Views is the total view count; Likes is the like count.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_superchat: Fires when a viewer sends a SuperChat in YouTube Live chat. User is the sender; Message is the attached text; Amount and Currency carry the purchase value (e.g. 5.00 and "USD"); Tier is YouTube's internal amount tier.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_superstick: Fires when a viewer sends a SuperSticker in YouTube Live chat. Amount and Currency carry the purchase value; StickerAlt is the sticker's alt text; StickerUrl is its image URL.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_timeout: Times User out of your YouTube live chat for Sec seconds. Sec defaults to 300; values below 1 are rejected.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_userbanned: Fires when a user is banned from YouTube Live chat. User is who got banned; BanType distinguishes permanent from temporary bans; Duration is the length in seconds for temporary ones.
architect.node.bubble.youtube_usertimedo: Fires when a user is timed out in YouTube Live chat. User is who got timed out; Duration is the timeout length in seconds. Requires Streamer.bot 1.0.5 or newer.
visualist.canvas.status.audioRequired: The Audio.Play sink cannot be deleted from the canvas — remove the upstream wire instead if you want no audio.
visualist.canvas.status.displayRequired: The Display sink is required and cannot be deleted.
visualist.node.bubble.audio_load: Loads an audio clip from disk for playback. Wire its Audio output into an Audio.Play sink — audio is not drawable, so wiring it into Display does nothing.
visualist.node.bubble.audio_play: Plays the wired Audio input through the OBS browser source. Volume is 0..1 (full by default); enable Loop for music/ambience, leave it off for one-shot SFX.
visualist.node.bubble.caption_livecaptio: WARNING: the LiveCaption feed is single-stream — only one Caption.LiveCaption widget per layer will receive captions at a time. Multiple Caption.LiveCaption widgets in the same layer will conflict. Outputs the original transcript and a Translated string (equal to the original when TargetLang is empty). PreviewText drives the design-time placeholder so the canvas thumbnail isn't blank.
visualist.node.bubble.color_constant: Outputs a fixed color value (hex string like "#ff8800"). Feed it into Text.Render or anywhere a Color socket is required.
visualist.node.bubble.display: The terminal sink — whatever Image you wire into it gets drawn into the widget's rect in OBS. Auto-injected into every widget graph; the canvas walks upstream from here at evaluation time.
visualist.node.bubble.image_blend: Composites image B (top) over image A (bottom) using a standard CSS blend mode (multiply, screen, overlay, etc.). Opacity (0..1) controls how strongly B shows through. Both A and B are required. Pipeline slot: LAST visual op before Display.
visualist.node.bubble.image_coloradjust: Per-source colour grading: Hue (degrees), Saturation, Brightness, and Contrast (each -1..1, 0 = no change; -1 saturation = greyscale). Pipeline slot: AFTER Crop, BEFORE Transform — so rotation/scale don't bake into colour samples.
visualist.node.bubble.image_combine: Like Image.Blend but adds three key modes that derive alpha from B's pixel values: alpha-key (B's existing alpha), luminance-key (black → transparent), inv-luminance (white → transparent). Convenient when chaining shape generators (Mask.Rectangle, Mask.Circle, etc.) without juggling separate Blend + Mask nodes.
visualist.node.bubble.image_crop: Clips the input image to the rectangle Rect (Vector4: X, Y, W, H, in source-image pixels). Wire from a Vector.Rect4 / Vector4.Constant for clarity. Pipeline slot: FIRST after Load.
visualist.node.bubble.image_load: Loads an image from disk so it can be drawn onto the layer. Set Path to a file under the data/media folder. First step of the canonical pipeline (Load → Crop → ColorAdjust → Transform → Tile → Mask → Blend → Display).
visualist.node.bubble.image_loadurl: Loads an image from a remote URL through the Hub asset proxy. Use for live thumbnails, avatars, or anything served over HTTP. Output is an Image you can chain into Crop, Transform, ColorAdjust, etc.
visualist.node.bubble.image_mask: Cuts the Image input through a Mask input — pixels where the mask is opaque (or bright, in luminance mode) survive; the rest go transparent. Both inputs are required. Mode = "alpha" (default) reads the mask's alpha channel; "luminance" uses brightness instead. Pipeline slot: AFTER ColorAdjust / Transform, BEFORE Blend.
visualist.node.bubble.image_scale: Scales the input image by Factor (1 = identity, <1 shrinks, >1 enlarges). Factor can be wired from a Scalar source or set inline. Often the easiest way to grow/shrink a logo without touching Transform.
visualist.node.bubble.image_tile: Tiles the input image across the widget rect, repeating Repeat.X times horizontally and Repeat.Y times vertically. Output dimensions match the widget's bounds (the tile fills the widget). Pipeline slot: AFTER Transform, BEFORE Mask / Blend.
visualist.node.bubble.image_transform: Translates, rotates, and scales the input image. Translate is a Vector2 in pixels; Rotate is degrees; Scale is a per-axis Vector2 multiplier. Pipeline slot: AFTER Crop / ColorAdjust, BEFORE Tile / Mask / Blend.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_bezier: Generates a curved polygon mask from a list of bezier vertices (each carrying two control points). Edit via the ShapeEditor modal — there's no inline pill. Use for organic shapes the polygon mask can't hit.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_circle: Generates a circular mask centred at (CX, CY) with the given Radius — all in normalised 0..1 layer space. Feather softens the edge; Inverted swaps inside/outside. Output is an Image.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_ellipse: Generates an ellipse mask with independent RadiusX / RadiusY and an optional Rotation (degrees). All coordinates are normalised 0..1 of the layer. Output is an Image.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_lineargradien: Generates a linear alpha gradient from (FromX, FromY) at FromAlpha to (ToX, ToY) at ToAlpha. All coordinates are normalised 0..1 of the layer. Use as a soft mask for fades and reveals.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_polygon: Generates a straight-edged polygon mask from a list of vertices (normalised 0..1 layer space). Edit the Vertices list via the ShapeEditor modal — there's no inline pill. Closed = true joins the last vertex back to the first.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_radialgradien: Generates a radial alpha gradient centred at (CX, CY), going from InnerAlpha at InnerRadius out to OuterAlpha at OuterRadius. All radii / coords are normalised 0..1 of the layer. Useful for spotlights and soft vignettes.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_rectangle: Generates a rectangle mask (Image output). All coordinates are normalised 0..1 of the layer. CornerRadius rounds the corners; Feather softens the edge; Inverted flips opaque/transparent. Wire into Image.Mask's Mask socket or into Image.Combine.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_star: Generates a star-shaped mask with Points tips (3..16) alternating between OuterRadius and InnerRadius. Rotation, Feather and Inverted work like the other Mask shapes. All coords are normalised 0..1 of the layer.
visualist.node.bubble.mask_vignette: One-knob preset for the classic vignette look — internally renders a Mask.RadialGradient with canonical defaults driven by Strength (0..1, higher = darker corners). Compose with Image.Blend in multiply mode over your image.
visualist.node.bubble.math_add: Adds two scalars: Out = A + B.
visualist.node.bubble.math_clamp: Clamps V to the range [Min, Max]. Use this when an upstream Math chain can drift outside 0..1 before feeding an Opacity / Brightness socket.
visualist.node.bubble.math_div: Divides two scalars: Out = A ÷ B. Returns 0 when B is 0 instead of erroring.
visualist.node.bubble.math_lerp: Linear interpolation between A and B by T (0 = A, 1 = B). T is conventionally 0..1; values outside the band extrapolate.
visualist.node.bubble.math_lerpvector2: Per-component linear interpolation between two Vector2 values by scalar T (0 = A, 1 = B). T is conventionally 0..1.
visualist.node.bubble.math_lerpvector3: Per-component linear interpolation between two Vector3 values by scalar T (0 = A, 1 = B). T is conventionally 0..1.
visualist.node.bubble.math_lerpvector4: Per-component linear interpolation between two Vector4 values by scalar T (0 = A, 1 = B). T is conventionally 0..1.
visualist.node.bubble.math_mul: Multiplies two scalars: Out = A × B. Handy for opacity attenuation (e.g. fade × pulse).
visualist.node.bubble.math_resolution: Outputs the active layer's resolution as a Vector2 (Width, Height). Use it to scale or position widgets relative to the layer size.
visualist.node.bubble.math_sub: Subtracts two scalars: Out = A − B.
visualist.node.bubble.result_if: Branch gate between an Image source and Display. Compares eventData[When] (e.g. "Args1") against Equals; on match, In passes through to Out — on mismatch (or if the named arg is missing) the branch is blocked and emits no image. Compose multiple Result.If nodes in parallel for mutually-exclusive routes (e.g. gamble outcome → win/loss/draw image).
visualist.node.bubble.scalar_constant: Outputs a fixed scalar number, normalised 0..1 by convention (1 = full, 0 = none). Use as an Opacity, Factor, Brightness, etc. driver. Values outside 0..1 are accepted; downstream kernels decide whether to clamp.
visualist.node.bubble.text_render: Rasterises a string into an Image so text can flow through the standard Image pipeline (Mask, Blend, Display). Set FontSize, FontFamily, Color, and Alignment (left / center / right). Output is Image.
visualist.node.bubble.text_translate: Translates Text into TargetLang via the Hub-routed translation service. Results are cached per (text, targetLang) so repeated frames don't refire round-trips.
visualist.node.bubble.vector2_constant: Outputs a fixed 2-component vector (X, Y). Useful for Image.Transform Translate/Scale or any Vector2 input.
visualist.node.bubble.vector3_combine: Packs three scalars X, Y, Z into a single Vector3 value.
visualist.node.bubble.vector3_constant: Outputs a fixed 3-component vector (X, Y, Z). Pairs with Math.LerpVector3 and the Vector3.Split / Combine nodes.
visualist.node.bubble.vector3_split: Splits a Vector3 into its X, Y, Z scalar components.
visualist.node.bubble.vector4_combine: Packs four scalars X, Y, Z, W into a single Vector4 value.
visualist.node.bubble.vector4_constant: Outputs a fixed 4-component vector (X, Y, Z, W). Use Vector.Rect4 if you want X/Y/W/H labels for crop rectangles instead.
visualist.node.bubble.vector4_split: Splits a Vector4 into its X, Y, Z, W scalar components.
visualist.node.bubble.vector_combine: Packs two scalars X and Y into a single Vector2 value.
visualist.node.bubble.vector_rect4: Friendly alias for a Vector4 with X/Y/W/H labels. Wire its Rect output into Image.Crop or anywhere a rectangle is expected.
visualist.node.bubble.vector_split: Splits a Vector2 into its X and Y scalar components.
visualist.node.bubble.video_load: Plays a local video file as an animated Image source. Set Path to a file under data/media. Defaults to muted + looped so OBS browser-source autoplay works without user interaction. Outputs Image (the current frame) and Duration in seconds.
visualist.node.bubble.viewer: Passthrough debug node — drop it on any wire and the value flows through unchanged so the chain keeps working. Future builds will paint a live thumbnail in the node body; today it shows a checker-pattern placeholder.
visualist.node.bubble.visual_complete: Lifecycle sink — when graph evaluation reaches this node, the compositor signals VISUAL_COMPLETE back to Hub so any wait_for_visual script proceeds on its Done branch. The Image input is for symmetry with Display; its value is not rendered. If a graph has no Visual.Complete, the engine falls back to firing on the first Display render.
visualist.node.bubble.visual_onstartup: Fires once when the layer activates in OBS. Outputs the LayerId (string) and a Timestamp (seconds). Use it to seed widgets that should render immediately on layer load.
visualist.node.bubble.visual_ontrigger: Entry point for a widget trigger. Outputs the trigger context that arrived from Hub: TriggerName, EventData (raw JSON), UserName, and Message. The Name attribute selects which named trigger this node listens for (e.g. "onTrigger:hype").
